newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia pres Tudjman sees 6-7.0 pct 1997 GDP rise.
newsitem.headline: Croatia pres Tudjman sees 6-7.0 pct 1997 GDP rise.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman said on Wednesday economic and investment growth remained primary goals in 1997.

"Last year's rise in gross domestic product (GDP) is estimated at around 7.0 percent, which is one of the highest growth rates among transition countries," Tudjman said in his annual 'state of the nation' address to the parliament.

"For this year, we expect continuing growth at a rate between 6.0 and 7.0 percent," he said, adding Croatia should strive to keep the rate high in the next 10-20 years "to get closer to West European countries."
Some leading economists were less optimistic and recently forecasted lower 1997 growth at 5.5 percent due to uncertain export demand.
But Tudjman said 1997 exports would hover around $4.6 billion and imports around $7.5 billion. He also expected a trade deficit between $2.8-2.9 billion, similarly to 1996.
He noted that foreign investments were rising, totalling $400 million in 1996.
Last week, Croatia was awarded favourable credit ratings, which should help it attract more foreign investment from abroad.
